Items.Authors: Charles-Antoine Claveau, Hannah Gulick, Jessica R. Lu, Kodi Rider, Steven V. W. Beckwith, Josh Bloom, Sharon R. Jelinsky, Matt Dexter, Wei Liu, Dan Werthimer
Items.Title: CuRIOS-ED: optical AIT workflow and on-ground performance characterization of a 12U CubeSat imaging payload
Items.Abstract: CuRIOS-ED (CubeSats for Rapid Infrared and Optical Surveys – Exploration Demo) is a 12U CubeSat payload and pathfinder for the CuRIOS constellation, a fleet of CubeSats for optical monitoring of the transient sky. The payload combines a commercial Simera f/6 telescope with a Sony IMX455 CMOS detector in a custom camera housing. The system delivers a 3° field of view. We present the optical AIT workflow and on-ground performance of the telescope–detector assembly. A metrology-based alignment scheme positions the focal plane within the ±50 µm depth of focus, with a mean focus error <5 µm across the 36×24 mm sensor. End-to-end tests on a clean-room bench, using a custom OAP collimator, yield PSFs with core FWHM ≲1 pixel (<1.5″), consistent with the vendor wavefront map. PSF mapping after qualification-level vibration shows no measurable degradation, indicating that the CuRIOS-ED optical payload meets its image-quality budget and is robust against launch loads.

Items.Authors: Tomoya Hori, Koji S. Kawabata, Kohji Tsumura, Daisuke Yonetoku, Hideo Matsuhara, Shuji Matsuura, Hiroshi Akitaya, Akihiro Doi, Satoru Endo
Items.Title: Current development status of Kösters prism for MONSTER onboard HiZ-GUNDAM satellite
Items.Abstract: The concept of the HiZ-GUNDAM satellite is to search transients, including gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), with the wide-field X-ray monitor (EAGLE), and then perform autonomous follow-up observations of these objects using the visible and NIR telescope (MONSTER). The MONSTER adopts the Kösters prism for split NIR observation band 0.9-2.5μm into four bands and perform imaging observations simultaneously with a single NIR detector.  We have developed a double Kösters prism and are currently conducting tests and performance evaluations. As a performance evaluation, we tested cooling, irradiation and vibration resistance of adhesive using prism’s bonding points and we designed holding mechanism of prism and detector. Furthermore, we simply measured transmittance of each band of prism. I will describe on the development status and performance evaluation test results of the Kösters prism.

Items.Authors: Mehmet Kuruçolak, Ebru Uzunçam, Hüseyin Araz Ağdamli, Onur Şatır, Cahit Yeşilyaprak
Items.Title: DAG - HVAC control system: ventilation strategies for thermal performance of primary mirror on the DAG400 telescope
Items.Abstract: This study examines the operational processes of the integrated HVAC (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning) system of the DAG400 telescope and the cooling steps of its primary mirror. The functions of the system components, their impacts on observation operations, and their operational scenarios are detailed.  The impact of the thermal management strategy on mirror seeing was quantified by comparing wavefront error (WFE) measurements under various conditions. The results confirm that autonomous HVAC preconditioning systems are an inevitable architectural requirement. Accordingly, the system's interfaces with observation operations and external systems must be accurately analyzed, and the system configuration should be structured based on this framework. These systems are of critical importance for mitigating mirror seeing effects in large class monolithic mirror telescopes, particularly in environments subject to high day to night temperature variations.

Items.Authors: Kirill Makan, Anastasia Galkin, Jochen Klar
Items.Title: Daiquiri: a framework for publishing astronomical data
Items.Abstract: At the Leibniz Institute for Astrophysics Potsdam (AIP), the Daiquiri framework and the containerized envi-  ronment dq-dev are used to host, curate, and publish large astrophysical data sets. Dedicated web applications  allow scientists to access SQL databases through browser-based interfaces and services implementing Interna-  tional Virtual Observatory Alliance (IVOA) standards, such as the Table Access Protocol (TAP) and DataLink.  The framework supports data delivery in formats such as FITS, VOTable, and Apache Parquet, and provides in-  tegrated user management, group-based access control, metadata curation, and metadata harvesting capabilities.  Daiquiri is open-source software available at https://github.com/django-daiquiri/daiquiri.    This manuscript focuses on the publication tasks that arise once scientific data are available and science-  ready.

Items.Authors: Xinyu Yao, Jian Ge, Quanquan Hu, Yan Li, Jianqing Cai, Pengjun Zhang, Kevin Willis
Items.Title: Data analysis of laboratory photometry experiments with GSENSE 1081BSI CMOS Detectors
Items.Abstract: The Earth 2.0 (ET) mission, led by China, aims to detect over 50000 exoplanets, including potentially habitable Earth-like planets around Sun-like stars (“Earth 2.0s”), cold low-mass planets, and free-floating planets. The mission will employ six 28-cm telescopes to conduct ultra-high-precision photometric monitoring for the detection of transiting planets. To verify that the telescopes can reliably detect exoplanet transit events, we have developed a high-precision photometry testbed. This system evaluates selected CMOS detectors for their ability to detect Earth 2.0 transit signals, specifically those exhibiting photometric variations at the 84-ppm level. This report presents the laboratory data processing and analysis pipeline. Preliminary results show that, for simulated sources equivalent to a 12.5-mag Sun-like star, a photometric precision of 10 ppm can be achieved over a 6.5-hour timescale. Moreover, we have successfully recovered injected Earth 2.0-like transit signals.

Items.Authors: Mieke Bouwhuis, Karl Kosack, Maximilian Linhoff
Items.Title: Data processing and preservation for the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory
Items.Abstract: We present the data processing and preservation system for the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO). The CTAO is the next-generation very-high-energy gamma-ray observatory currently under construction at Paranal (Chile) and Observatory Roque de los Muchachos (La Palma, Spain). The data processing system handles the transfer of the petabytes of data generated by the Observatory and processes them into science-ready data products. The system also performs data qualification of low-level data from the Observatory and generates and processes simulation data required to model the instrument response. The data are processed in parallel workflows across different CTAO data centers and are managed at large scale at distributed locations. We describe the infrastructure used for preservation of the data and for execution of the data processing workflows.

Items.Authors: Andre Fogal, William Thompson, Christian Marois, Joeleff Fitzsimmons, Kaitlyn Hessel, Adam Johnson, Olivier Lardière, Christopher Mann
Items.Title: Deep learning wavefront reconstruction on-sky: results from the SPIDERS Lyot-based low order wavefront sensor
Items.Abstract: The Subaru Pathfinder Instrument for Detecting Exoplanets and Retrieving Spectra (SPIDERS) uses a Lyot-based Low Order Wavefront Sensor (LLOWFS) to perform pupil-plane wavefront sensing. Currently, wavefront reconstruction relies on a linear reconstructor, but this approach struggles with the inherently nonlinear nature of the problem, leading to instability and crosstalk between modes, adding additional signal that must be corrected by the LLOWFS. To address this, we have developed a machine learning-based wavefront reconstructor based on a convolutional neural network (CNN). The CNN is trained on SPIDERS bench data, increasing the linear range of the LLOWFS and leading to more effective wavefront control. We will present results demonstrating the CNN's performance in on-sky operation from the recent deployment of SPIDERS on the Subaru telescope. This approach is broadly applicable to low-order wavefront sensing and can help drive contrasts lower as we search for other worlds.

Items.Authors: Benedetta Di Francesco, Stefano Di Frischia, Ivan Di Antonio, Gianluca Di Rico
Items.Title: Deep learning wavefront sensing with multimode fibers : from numerical simulations to experimental implementation
Items.Abstract: The synergy between astronomy and photonics is offering new perspectives in the field of wavefront sensing for ground-based telescopes. In this context, the integration of photonic devices and machine learning is particularly promising. Within this framework, this research investigates the use of multimode fibers (MMFs) as wavefront sensors, combined with a properly trained Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Aberrated wavefronts were propagated through a simulated multimode fiber with known properties, and the resulting intensity patterns were used for network training. Following this simulation phase, an optical bench has been developed to experimentally verify the concept and evaluate its performance under controlled laboratory conditions. This step marks a crucial transition from numerical modeling to physical implementation, enabling future developments and experimental validation.

Items.Authors: Jonathan Dray, Morgan Gray, Baptiste Sinquin, Jalo Nousiainen, Cédric Taïssir Héritier Salama, Hisham Forriere, Julien Charton, Armin Schimpf, Thierry Fusco, Benoit Neichel
Items.Title: Deep learning-based reconstructor coupled with reinforcement learning for adaptive optics in LEO optical links
Items.Abstract: In this work, we present a reconstruction pipeline for LEO satellite free-space optical communications, combining a CNN-based deep learning reconstructor with the predictive PO4AO controller. We show that the CNN outperforms classical reconstruction methods under low-photon-flux and high-scintillation conditions. Closed-loop simulations at kilohertz rates demonstrate improved fiber coupling efficiency compared to classical Karhunen–Loève reconstruction across varying elevation angles and Rytov variances. This approach highlights the benefit of integrating deep learning upstream of model-based predictive control for challenging adaptive optics scenarios.

Items.Authors: Camila Solar, Francisco Oyarzún, Camilo Weinberger, Matthias Schreiber, Esteban Vera, Jorge Tapia
Items.Title: Deep-learning-enhanced pyramid wavefront sensor in free-space optical communication scenarios
Items.Abstract: The rise of digital technologies demand high-fidelity, high-bandwidth communication systems. In this context, free-space optical communication (FSOC) emerges as an alternative to traditional radiofrequency (RF) links. However, atmospheric turbulence distorts the phase of the transmitted light signal. These distortions are corrected by adaptive optics (AO) systems which are based on the use of wavefront sensors (WFSs). In FSOC applications, the Shack–Hartmann wavefront sensor (SHWFS) is typically employed but owing to scintillation, it has problems in the phase-measuring process, risking quality of the coupling. In this work we evaluate the performance of the non-modulated pyramidal wavefront sensor (PWFS) under FSOC conditions and boost its functioning using deep learning tools. As a result, a comparison of the closed-loop performance of the SHWFS and PWFS will be presented using metrics related to FSOC and AO systems, aiming to explore the PWFS as a potential alternative for FSOC.

Items.Authors: Peyton Benac, Michael P. Fitzgerald, Eric Wang, Chris Johnson, Andrew J. Skemer, Philip Hinz, Nick MacDonald, Dale Sandford, R. Deno Stelter, Brittany Miles, Markus Loose, Richard Blank, Thomas Greene, Steph Sallum, William Deich, Dusty Reichwein, Aaron Hunter, Athira Unni
Items.Title: Demonstration of a hybrid fast/slow readout mode for the H2RG detectors in SCALES
Items.Abstract: The upcoming SCALES instrument for W.M. Keck Observatory will enable imaging and low-/mid-resolution coronagraphic integral field spectroscopic observations over 1-5 micron wavelengths, using two separate HgCdTe Teledyne Imaging H2RG detectors. These detectors are wired for slow-mode readout with 4 output channels at a pixel clock rate of ~100kHz, but when operated with a Teledyne Imaging SIDECAR ASIC followed by an AstroBlank/Markury Scientific MACIE controller card, the system can be operated at faster clock rates up to 1.8 MHz to avoid saturation on bright backgrounds—a mode referred to as hybrid fast-slow readout. We demonstrate cryogenic performance with the H2RG detectors in the complete SCALES instrument and characterize the detectors’ full-frame data acquisition performance in hybrid mode with pixel clock rates from 0.2-1.8 MHz. We present results obtained during detector system testing at UC Santa Cruz, and discuss next steps for commissioning.

Items.Authors: Yu Ning, Hao-ran Ma, Wang Yu, Hai-feng Xu, Wen-qing Qu, Hong-fei Zhang, Jian Wang
Items.Title: Design and characterization of an InGaAs near-infrared camera
Items.Abstract: InGaAs focal plane arrays exhibit high responsivity in the 0.9-1.7um near-infrared bands and are widely used in near-infrared imaging, laser detection, spectral measurement, semiconductor inspection, and astronomical observation. To meet the requirements of stable imaging and low-noise readout for InGaAs focal plane arrays, a near-infrared camera based on a 640 *512 InGaAs focal plane array detector with a 15um pixel pitch developed by the Kunming Institute of Physics was designed and implemented in this work. The camera mainly consists of a preamplifier board, a main control board, a TEC control board, and a power board. In this paper we focus on the overall camera structure and electronics architecture design and presents a preliminary performance evaluation of the camera, which can provide a reference for the development of InGaAs near-infrared imaging systems.

Items.Authors: Giulia Mattioli, Enrico Virgilli, Claudio Labanti, Lorenzo Amati, Giuseppe Baldazzi, Giuseppe Bertuccio, Edoardo Borciani, Riccardo Campana, Paolo Calabretto, Francesca Di Leo, Evgeny Demenev, Francesco Ficorella, Mauro Fiorini, Marco Grassi, Giovanni La Rosa, Piero Malcovati, Filippo Mele, Valerio Messina, Paolo Nogara, David Novel, Luca Nunziante, Giancarlo Pepponi, Paolo Sarra, Smiriti Srivastava
Items.Title: Design and characterization of the XGIS Detection Plane Demonstration Module (DPDM)
Items.Abstract: The X and Gamma-ray Imaging Spectrometer (XGIS) on THESEUS is designed to detect and localize transient X-ray and gamma-ray sources from 2 keV to 10 MeV, enabling high-resolution timing and spectroscopy for time-domain and multi-messenger astrophysics. It uses two identical coded-mask cameras imaging up to 150 keV and monitoring higher energies. The detection plane is built from thousands of modular elements, each a CsI(Tl) scintillator bar read by Silicon Drift Detectors (SDDs), offering broad-band coverage in a compact design. Recent developments include testing of SDDs and scintillator assemblies, ASIC prototype validation, and optimization of the electronic architecture, leading to the Detection Plane Demonstration Module (DPDM) developed by OHB-Italia with academic and research partners. This contribution presents the DPDM design, updated architecture, and performance tests within the THESEUS M7 Phase A.

Items.Authors: Hiroto Shimizu, Hikaru Munemura, Shohei Kusuda, Hiroshi Nakajima, Yuki K. Satoh, Koichi Hagino, Daiki Ishi, Masaki Numazawa, Yuichiro Ezoe, Kumi Ishikawa, Junko S. Hiraga
Items.Title: Design and development of focal plane CMOS camera onboard GEO-X (GEOspace X-ray imager)
Items.Abstract: We report the latest performance of the focal plane CMOS camera onboard the GEO-X (GEO-space X-ray imager) mission. The back-illuminated CMOS sensor has high sensitivity in the energy band from 0.3 to 2.0 keV and moderate energy resolution of 120eV (FWHM) at 0.6 keV. It is cooled down to -20 ℃ with Peltier cooler to reduce the dark noise. We have designed the camera body as a radiation shield and the vent pipe with the sufficient attenuation performance of intruding visible light. The developing status such as functional test including backend electronics and environmental tests will also be presented.

Items.Authors: Rodrigo Muñoz, Nicolas Hernández, Felipe Guzman, Esteban Vera
Items.Title: Design and experimental implementation of deep holographic Fourier-plane wavefront sensors
Items.Abstract: We present the design and experimental implementation of deep holographic Fourier-plane wavefront sensors for astronomy and free-space optics. Pyramid-like Fourier elements are encoded as low-cost holograms by computing their phase, generating an off-axis computer-generated hologram, and recording it from an SLM onto a holographic plate with a 4f system. On the bench, an SLM generates atmospheric phase screens with controlled r0, while the holographic Fourier sensor measures the distorted wavefront. A transformer neural network is first trained on simulated data and then refined with a mix of simulated and experimental images, learning a mapping from sensor images to Zernike modal coefficients. In closed loop, the SLM acts as a turbulence generator and an ALPAO deformable mirror provides correction. We report residual wavefront error and Strehl ratio for different turbulence strengths and discuss chromatic response and diffraction efficiency as key limitations for future improvements.

Items.Authors: Eduardo Medinaceli Villegas, Sebastiano Ligori, Vito Capobianco, Natalia Auricchio, Mauro Dadina, Marija Kuljanac, Gavin Walmsley
Items.Title: Design and functionalities of the instrument control unit of the New-Athena's X-IFU instrument
Items.Abstract: ESA's NewAthena mission proposal is under development and will undergo mission adoption in 2027. This general-purpose open X-ray observatory of the Hot and Energetic Universe will have an unprecedented combination of collective area, survey capabilities and energy resolution provided by the X-ray Integral Field Unit (X-IFU) instrument.  Here, the current preliminary design of the Instrument Control Unit (ICU) hardware and application software of X-IFU is presented. The ICU is part of a very complex SpaceWire network, the avionics architecture dealing with data harvesting, data buses and data handling, which defines the instrument capabilities, is governed by the ICU. The main ICU role is to handle all the data and generate the commands required onboard. It uses both a high-speed bus and a PPS signal to orchestrate the control of the instrument. All ICU functionalities will be implemented in the ASW running in the state-of-the-art processor, based on a preemptive multi-task architecture.

Items.Authors: Qi Feng, Hong-fei Zhang, Jian Wang, Zi-yi Liu, Baolong Chen, Kang-zhe Wang, Kangzhe Wang, Xing-bo Wang, Yi-xin Liu, Zhe Geng, Song-hao Li, Qiang Wu
Items.Title: Design and progress of the CMOS Mosaic Camera for Earth 2.0's microlensing telescope
Items.Abstract: The Exoplanet Earth Science Survey Satellite (Earth 2.0) is planned to be deployed in a halo orbit around the Sun–Earth L2 point. It will function as a space observatory consisting of six wide - field transit telescopes and one microlensing telescope. By combining the transit and microlensing methods, it will conduct a large - scale survey of terrestrial planets and free - floating planets. The microlensing CMOS camera is assembled from four 9K×9K detectors tiled together with guiding detectors. When combined with high - precision thermal control and readout electronics, it can achieve highly stable photometry with a single - exposure signal-to-noise ratio ≥ 5 for targets of 20.5 magnitude. The relevant key technologies have been validated using a prototype camera, which demonstrates that they meet the requirements of both scientific observations and engineering implementation.

Items.Authors: Chenlong Li, Hualin Chen, Jiaxin Li, Hua Bai
Items.Title: Design of a conical phase optical system for RINGSS
Items.Abstract: Given that the Ring-Image Next Generation Scintillation Sensor (RINGSS) can provide long-term, high-precision   atmospheric optical turbulence parameter data for astronomical observatory sites, this paper presents a design study of a conical phase optical system for RINGSS. By introducing a virtual phase compensation surface in front of the telescope, we designed either a rear air-spaced spherical lens group or a rear axicon capable of generating a conical phase distribution. The study demonstrates that an approximate conical phase can be realized by combining the spherical aberration term—i.e., the 11th Zernike polynomial coefficient—with telescope defocus, enabling the optimization of a rear air-spaced spherical lens group. Conversely, an exact conical phase is achieved through employing the first-order term of odd-aspheric surfaces to design a rear axicon. The resulting optical systems produce high-quality, achromatic ring images across the 400–800 nm wavelength range.

Items.Authors: Song-hao Li, Hang Zhan, Qi Feng, Xingbo Wang, Zi-yi Liu, Hong-fei Zhang, Jian Wang
Items.Title: Design of sCMOS Test Camera and its Radiation Test for Aerospace Applications
Items.Abstract: The harsh space radiation environment poses significant challenges to the reliability of detector systems, making the on-orbit validation of high-performance and robust CMOS image sensors a critical step for aerospace applications. We will present the design and systematic radiation testing of a prototype system based on the GSENSE1517BSI, a large-format, back-illuminated CMOS detector, developed for such demanding environments. To evaluate its performance and radiation tolerance, we developed a prototype camera and conducted a series of tests, including proton and Co-60 γirradiation experiments under biased, low-temperature operating conditions, followed by annealing studies. We will detail the electronics of the camera and summarize test results of key parameters—such as gain, bias, readout noise, dark current, quantum efficiency, and full-well capacity—before and after irradiation, as well as after annealing.

Items.Authors: Hui Zhang, Bixuan Zhao, Chenliang Huang, Chenxu Gao, Zhaojun Yan, Wei Chen, Hongjing Yang, Weicheng Zang, Xinyu Yao, Maochun Wu, Jian Ge
Items.Title: Design of the ground data operation segment for the ET (Earth 2.0) mission
Items.Abstract: The ET mission will deliver unprecedented time-domain data sets for exoplanets and stellar astrophysics: six 28-cm transit telescopes downlink full-frame images at 15-minute cadence and postage stamps for selected targets, while a 35-cm microlensing telescope returns 10-minute cadence imaging toward the Galactic bulge. With a total data rate of 2500Gb per day and survey scales of >6 million FGKM dwarfs and >30 million bulge stars, the Ground Data Operation Segment (GDOS) is a critical element that transforms raw telemetry into validated science products and provides reliable, timely access for the community. This paper presents: (1) a science-driven requirements analysis; (2) the end-to-end ground processing flows for both the transit telescope array and the microlensing payload; and (3) the framework for the science database.

Items.Authors: Michael Gonzales, Andrew Skemer, R. Deno Stelter, Nicholas MacDonald, Basil Blank, Gerald Cabak, Guillaume Filion, Etienne Gauvin
Items.Title: Design, construction, and testing of the SCALES cryostat
Items.Abstract: SCALES (Slicer Combined with an Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy) is a 2–5 µm high-contrast, fully cryogenic integral field spectrograph and imager designed for operation behind the adaptive optics system at the W. M. Keck Observatory. The SCALES cryostat provides the stable, low-background environment required for high-sensitivity exoplanet characterization. It houses a large optomechanical payload cooled by two closed-cycle cryocoolers, with an internal liquid-nitrogen tank used to accelerate bench cooling at the start of each cooldown. This paper presents the assembly, pumpdown, and cryogenic tests of the SCALES cryostat, starting with an initial empty-cryostat run to validate vacuum integrity, thermal performance, and procedures. Subsequent cooldowns with progressively added mechanisms and optics achieved stable vacuum and an average bench temperature of about 80 K, demonstrating robust, repeatable performance that supports ongoing integration for future use at Keck.

Items.Authors: Sorabh Chhabra, Stefan Kraus, Jyotirmay Paul, Daniel Lancaster, Narsireddy Anugu, Michael J. Ireland, John D. Monnier, Owain Snaith
Items.Title: Design, integration, and commissioning of the BIFROST All-in-One 4-telescope Beam Combiner for 1.0–1.8 μm spectro-interferometry
Items.Abstract: The ASGARD/BIFROST instrument provides spectro-interferometric capability for the VLTI across the 1.0–1.8 μm wavelength range. Central to this system is the All-in-One (AIO) 4-telescope beam combiner, which integrates beam routing, spatial filtering, and spectrograph injection within a compact optomechanical assembly.  We present the optical and optomechanical design of the AIO combiner. The assembly and laboratory integration procedures are summarized, with emphasis on metrology, throughput verification, and fringe stability tests. Commissioning at the VLTI is reported with initial on-sky performance, including beam alignment, fringe acquisition, visibility calibration, and sensitivity across the Y–H bands.

Items.Authors: Dongok Ryu
Items.Title: Design-to-as-built distortion modeling of Korsch Telescopes for weak-lensing surveys
Items.Abstract: Weak gravitational lensing requires highly accurate galaxy shape measurements, making geometric distortion a critical systematic in wide-field space telescopes. Korsch TMAs offer excellent low-order aberration control but struggle to achieve the low distortion needed for weak-lensing surveys. This work addresses this challenge via three integrated approaches. First, a machine-learning framework identifies low-distortion solutions within wide-field Korsch design space. Second, an end-to-end observation model based on non-sequential ray tracing simulates intrinsic galaxy structure, weak-lensing shear, optical propagation, and pixel sampling in a unified 3D environment. Third, as-built mirrors generate a realistic distortion model. Comparing ML-derived designs and as-built data enables clearer separation of instrumental distortion from true gravitational shear, supporting distortion-controlled telescope development for future weak-lensing missions.

Items.Authors: Simon Tulloch, Jean Louis Lizon, Fujia Du
Items.Title: Detector System for the CHORUS high-resolution spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The CHORUS detector system consists of two 9k x 9k 16-output CCD9 and two 4k x 4k 4-output CCD4. These four detectors are read out using three STA Archon controllers with identical hardware configurations. Differential preamplifiers with active baseline restoration are used for low-crosstalk, low-noise performance with improved linearity. Preamplifier modules have been manufactured that mount directly onto the hermetic cryostat connectors. Rigiflex PCB technology is used for all vacuum-side cabling. This gives higher reliability as well as the opportunity to place ESD-protection and bias-decoupling components close to the detectors.

Items.Authors: Malhar Sonaniskar, Douglas Neill, Ellie Hileman, Petr Kubánek
Items.Title: Determining stress-based bending mode limits for the Vera C. Rubin Observatory M1M3 active mirror system
Items.Abstract: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory's primary-tertiary mirror (M1M3) is a monolithic 8.4-m borosilicate mirror supported by 156 pneumatic actuators. Because the mirror is irreplaceable, glass safety is a hard constraint on every actuator command. Full FEA provides accurate stress predictions but is too slow for real-time control.    This work presents a rapid stress-estimation method based on Root-Sum-Square (RSS) combination of pre-computed unit bending mode stresses. RSS predictions are validated against NASTRAN FEA for ten realistic multi-mode correction trials. Agreement is within ±5% for 7 of 10 trials. A 1.25× safety factor provides a conservative operational bound across all cases. Direct summation overestimates FEA by 101–302%, rendering it unworkable. The method evaluates in microseconds, enabling real-time stress monitoring at full telescope control.

Items.Authors: Natasha Carr, Charly H. Feldman, Simon T. Lindsay, Adrian Martindale, Will Dunn, Bryn Parry, Jonathan Nichols, Sam Wharton, George Clark
Items.Title: Developing a novel in situ x-ray telescope for a Jovian mission
Items.Abstract: The Jovian system provides a multitude of X-ray sources, including emissions from the diffuse radiation belt and Io plasma torus, atmospheric and auroral emissions and plasma-surface interactions with the Galilean moons. In-situ observations will provide fluxes in the range of 10^4-10^6 ph/s, allowing for full characterisation of X-ray emissions.  We present an X-ray instrument concept for a Jupiter mission. The 6 x 6 MPO array and 630mm focal length provides a 19 degree field-of-view and a <1000km resolution at 5 Jupiter radii. This concept draws on the extensive history and heritage of lobster eye telescopes developed at the University of Leicester.

Items.Authors: Laurent Ravera, Yann Parot, Thierry Camus, Odile Coeur-Joly, Corentin Guerin, David Murat, Loïc Noguès, Jan Soucek, Radek Lan, Ludek Uhlir, Frédéric Pinsard, Charles Boreux, Christophe Cara, Marcelo Braga E Silva, Frédéric Chateau, Maité Ceballos, Beatriz Cobo, Nicolás Cardiel, David Granena, Denis Schwander, Etienne Pointecouteau
Items.Title: Development and demonstration results of the digital readout electronics for the NewAthena X-IFU instrument
Items.Abstract: The Digital Readout Electronics (DRE) plays a critical role in signal acquisition and processing from the Transition Edge Sensor (TES) array. Developed for Time Domain Multiplexing (TDM) readout, this system builds on experience from Frequency Domain Multiplexing prototypes and addresses the challenges specific to high-resolution X-ray detection. The DRE is responsible for generating row selection signals, sampling pixel error outputs, and producing feedback and dynamic offset compensation signals to ensure accurate readout from the MUX SQUIDs. It performs real-time event detection, extracting 8192-sample data records at a sampling frequency of 130.2 kHz, and processes them to determine photon arrival time, energy, and event grade. Final photon energy values are calibrated on-ground using gain scale corrections.

Items.Authors: Chris A. S. Parmenter, Nick R. Waltham, Matthew J. Clapp, Téa Seitis, Matthew Tildesley, Matt Beasley, Todd J. Veach, Craig DeForest
Items.Title: Development and planned evolution of CCD camera electronics for the PUNCH wide field and narrow field Imagers
Items.Abstract: The Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere (PUNCH) mission is a constellation of four satellites imaging the Sun in visible light from a Sun-synchronous low Earth orbit. It aims to improve our understanding of how the solar wind transitions from the Sun’s corona to the heliosphere.    We present the development and characterisation of the CCD camera electronics common to the Wide Field Imager (WFI) and Narrow Field Imager (NFI) instruments for the PUNCH mission, which include RAL’s custom Correlated Double Sampling (CDS) Analogue-to-Digital Converter (ADC) and Digital-to-Analogue Converter (DAC) ASICs. In addition, future technology developments to further increase the performance and reliability of the PUNCH camera electronics are summarised.

Items.Authors: Jing Guo, Yongtian Zhu, Jiangpei Dou, Xi Zhang, Zhen Wu, Mingming Xu, Gang Zhao, Gang Wang, Bo Chen, Huatao Zhang, Zhonghua Lv, Ruokun Li, Jinxin Chen, Yujia Cao
Items.Title: Development and testing of a ground-based high-contrast imager for exoplanet imaging
Items.Abstract: Detection and characterization of exoplanets is at one of the forefronts of astronomical research. Currently, ground-based high-contrast imaging instruments are available on highly competitive 8-10 meter class telescopes such as Gemini, VLT, Subaru and Keck. In this paper, a ground-based high-contrast imager developed by Nanjing Institute of Astronomical Optics & Technology, CAS (NIAOT) dedicated for exoplanet detection study is introduced. The instrument is optimized for medium-sized telescopes with an aperture size of 4-meter class and is designed to deliver an imaging contrast better than 10^(-5) in the near-infrared wavelengths. Testing results of the instrument show that its inner working angle is 0.51″ in J, H band and 0.79″ in Ks band, and an imaging contrast of 2.55×10^(-6), 4.06×10^(-7) and 8.46×10^(-7) is achieved in J, H and Ks band, respectively. Furthermore, preliminary trial observation results from the instrument on Lijiang 2.4-meter Telescope (LJT) are presented.

Items.Authors: Takahiro Nagayama, Hidehiko Nakaya
Items.Title: Development of 640×512 pixel InGaAs image sensors for H and Ks band astronomical observations
Items.Abstract: We are developing InGaAs image sensors for astronomical observations in  collaboration with Hamamatsu Photonics, Inc. (Japan). The sensors under  development features a pixel pitch of 20 μm and a total format of 640×512  pixels. The readout integrated circuit (ROIC) is a custom device newly  designed and optimized specifically for astronomical applications, and it  has already been completed and delivered.  Two types of InGaAs photodiode array are being prepared: one provides  sensitivity up to 2.1 μm at room temperature and is suitable for H band  observations, while the other offers sensitivity up to 2.6 μm at room  temperature for Ks band observations. In addition, a matured InGaAs photodiode  array with a 1.7 μm cutoff is being prepared for the J band. The hybridizations  of image sensors are scheduled to be completed in March 2026.  In this presentation, we will report on the fundamental performance  characteristics of these sensors.

Items.Authors: Chenhao Zhao, Yasuhiro Hirahara, Yuan Li, Biao Zhao, Shohei Negishi, Ryoichi Koga, Umi Enokidani, Hideo Matsuhara, Shunsuke Baba, Takao Nakagawa, Takehiko Wada
Items.Title: Development of a cryogenic high precision refractive index measurement system for CdZnTe using the minimum deviation method
Items.Abstract: We have developed a compact cryogenic system for high precision refractive index measurements of CdZnTe, aimed at supporting the optical design of the GREX PLUS high resolution spectrograph. The system is based on the minimum deviation method and incorporates improved vacuum rotation mechanics, non contact magnetic torque transfer, a low temperature ceramic thrust bearing, and flexible high purity copper thermal links. Together with narrow band mid infrared illumination and liquid nitrogen cooled InSb/MCT detectors using lock in detection, the setup enables stable angle measurements in the 4–20 K temperature range. The achieved accuracy of ∣δn∣<10^(-3) in the 10–18 µm wavelength region meets the requirements for designing high dispersion immersion gratings for space infrared instrumentation.

Items.Authors: S. Farina, L. Nassi, P. Nogara, L. Schettini, S. Incorvaia, S. D'Angelo, M. Fiorini, M. Carminati, G. Borghi, C. Fiorini, M. Uslenghi
Items.Title: Development of a high-dynamic range FUV photon counting detector prototype with a microchannel plate coupled to a low-noise custom readout ASIC
Items.Abstract: Microchannel-plate (MCP) detectors remain essential for far and extreme ultraviolet (FUV/EUV) astronomy thanks to their single-photon sensitivity and solar-blind response. In 2024, we developed a first prototype of an MCP readout based on a custom 32×32-pixel ASIC, integrating per-pixel charge shaping, event discrimination, and digital correction for charge sharing. This architecture achieves very low noise (~20 e⁻), enabling ALD MCPs to operate at low gain with high per-pixel count rates (up to 100 kcps). Building on these results, we are developing a second, improved version designed for larger detector formats, reduced power consumption, and enhanced robustness. The new system is currently under fabrication and will be tested in a dedicated UV vacuum chamber. This talk will summarize recent progress and outline future development paths.

Items.Authors: E. K. R. Floyd, I. Schofield, S. Rochelle, A. Haque, J. J. D. Luis, J. Altamirano, C. Salcido, J. Young, S. Norouzi
Items.Title: Development of an automated alignment system control software for the Magdalena Ridge Observatory Interferometer
Items.Abstract: To maximize science throughput at the Magdalena Ridge Observatory Interferometer (MROI), rapid and precise optical alignment is essential. This paper presents a scalable control interface designed to manage the facility's hardware, including motors, sources, and detectors. The architecture features an abstraction layer and a robust simulation mode that ensures system stability during hardware intermittency. Validated during MROI’s "First Fringes" on July 12, 2025, the system supports concurrent multi-user workflows to accelerate setup times. We discuss key lessons learned regarding the operator experience during on-sky commissioning and outline the roadmap for phased automation.

Items.Authors: Tushar Ubarhande, Suvendu Rakshit
Items.Title: Development of aperture masking interferometry for 13.7m National Large Optical Telescope (NLOT), India
Items.Abstract: Aperture masking interferometry (AMI) enables high-angular-resolution measurements by directly sampling spatial frequencies in the Fourier plane, providing visibility amplitudes and closure phases. We present the development of an AMI system intended for the proposed 13.7 m National Large Optical Telescope (NLOT), India, capable of achieving a theoretical resolution of ≈10 mas at 650 nm. Our work includes a flexible simulation framework for any telescope aperture, laboratory validation using interchangeable aperture masks, and on-sky testing with a 30 cm telescope. Simulations generate u–v coverage, visibilities, PSFs, and realistic noise to optimize mask design and predict telescope performance. Laboratory interferograms match simulations and help identify issues such as alignment and bandwidth smearing. Initial on-sky results confirm the reliability of the mask and visibility pipeline, and we are preparing to deploy a prototype on the 1.3 m DFOT (Devasthal Fast Optical Telescope).

Items.Authors: Ettore Del Monte, Matias Antonelli, Marco Grassi, Filippo Mele, Riccardo Campana, Francesco Ceraudo, Giovanni Della Casa, Giuseppe Di Persio, Yuri Evangelista, Mauro Fiorini, Alessio Nuti, Giulio Orzan, Alexander Rachevski, Irina Rashevskaya, Gianluigi Zampa, Nicola Zampa, Giuseppe Bertuccio, Irisa Dedolli, Piero Malcovati, Giancarlo Pepponi, Francesco Ficorella, Michele Caselle, Marco Feroci
Items.Title: Development of multipixel silicon drift detectors for x-rays
Items.Abstract: The Pixelated silicon Drift Detector (PixDD) is a multi-pixel X-ray sensor based on the silicon drift technology on a 2D matrix of pixels with 300 micrometers pitch. The front-end ASIC, named RIGEL, has a 2D matrix of cells with sparse readout, fast response time, and good noise performance even at room temperature. Sensor and ASIC are interfaced using a die-level bump bonding technique. PixDD is an ideal focal plane sensor for X-ray concentrators and lobster-eye optics.  An improvement of PixDD is the Imaging drift edgeless array for X-rays (IdeaX), recently approved in the framework of the PRORIS program. In IdeaX we plan to develop an edgeless system based on a pixelated silicon drift detector and two ASICs (front-end and back-end) interconnected using through-silicon vias and bump bonding. This approach aims to minimise the dead area on the focal plane.   Here we present the measured performance of the existing 16 x 16 pixels prototype of PixDD and we discuss the IdeaX working plan.

Items.Authors: Haruaki Niinuma, Hiroshi Akitaya, Shuichi Gunji, Yoshifusa Ita, Kohji Tsumura, Hideo Matsuhara, Daisuke Yonetoku
Items.Title: Development of onboard image processing software for MONSTER on the HiZ-GUNDAM satellite
Items.Abstract: HiZ-GUNDAM is a space mission designed to detect high-redshift gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) using both an X-ray telescope and a five-band visible/near-infrared telescope, MONSTER. Because the satellite’s real-time alert system cannot downlink raw images, image processing must be performed onboard. MONSTER detects roughly one thousand sources in the field of view, one of which is the GRB afterglow. Since transmitting information for all sources may be impossible, the system must identify only a few tens of afterglow candidates. To accomplish this, a lightweight decision-tree algorithm was developed that can run on the onboard computer. Using five-band photometric measurements, it narrows down the candidates to several tens. Using the constructed decision tree, when detector noise is ignored, the true afterglow at z > 6 is included among these selected candidates with nearly 100% probability. In this presentation, I will describe the details of this onboard candidate-selection algorithm.

Items.Authors: Bastián Romero, Felipe Guzmán, Esteban Vera
Items.Title: Development of real-time piston sensing using a single-shot coded aperture instrument and deep phase retrieval
Items.Abstract: We address ELT co-phasing challenges with a single-shot complex field wavefront sensor. Using coded diffraction intensity images, we detect piston discontinuities from segments and spiders. We employ deep learning enhanced phase retrieval to ensure high fidelity, bypassing iterative computational bottlenecks.

Items.Authors: Xiaofei Li, Xuhao Wu, Shidong Shen, Hua Bai, Yong Zhang, Dehua Yang, Xiangqun Cui
Items.Title: Development of Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensing for the 4m segmented JUST telescope
Items.Abstract: The JUST is a 4-m-class telescope. There are two main challenges for wavefront sensing in the JUST design. First, the secondary mirror and its baffle of up to approximately 1.8 m in diameter introduce a reduction of up to approximately 37% in the effective collecting area of the inner-ring segments. Second, the alt-azimuth mount causes continuous pupil rotation at the Nasmyth platforms during observation. To solve these issues, we design a switchable lenslet array mechanism and a mechanical pupil de-rotation assembly on the wide-field Nasmyth platform. We conducted estimation of reconstruction errors under prescribed centroid measurement errors of 1/20 and 1/30 pixel. The results show that the selected lenslet array sampling configuration can recover segment level low-order aberrations with residual wavefront errors at the ten nanometer scale for the obscured inner-ring segments.

Items.Authors: Yanji Yang, Jia Ma, Jiehan Cao, Jia Wang, Jixin Feng, Juncheng Lu, Qian Zhang, Yusa Wang, Yong Chen, Bo Wang, Dianlong Wang, Langping Wang, Fei Ding, Jiadai Xue, Pengfei Qiang, Yongqing Yan, Lizhi Sheng, Yupeng Xu
Items.Title: Development of the focusing mirrors onboard eXTP
Items.Abstract: The eXTP mission has finished the phase B study. The eXTP satellites employs 9 X-ray focusing mirrors including 6 mirrors with the reflective layer of gold and 3 with that of nickel. By the end of 2025, we have finished four phototypes of the mirror module employing the nickel replica technoloty. During the testing of the phototypes manufactured by Media Lario and us, we found additional loss of the effective area by 10%. In this way, we have rechecked the margin of the design of the effective area, and added 5 inner most shells into the mirror module to increase about 40 cm2. Moreover, the thickness to radius ratio has also increased to 0.002 to manufacture the mirror shells with higher yield rates.

Items.Authors: Charly Feldman, Alejandro Guzman, Roisin Ryan, Lauro Conti, Gillian Butcher, Anna Maskolenko, Paul Houghton, Stéphane Roose, Aline Hermans, Daniel Schuppe, Vadim Burwitz
Items.Title: Development of the THESEUS SXI optics for ESA M7 candidate
Items.Abstract: The University of Leicester and the University of Tuebingen as joint PI institutes for the Soft X-ray Instrument (SXI) on THESEUS, an ESA M7 candidate mission, are responsible for the optic and detector development. The SXI consists of two identical Lobster eye modules with an 8x8 array of Micro Pore Optics (MPO), working in the energy range 0.3-5 keV. We present the progress of the development of the breadboard optic, including frame material trade off, X-ray results of MPOs and the breadboard itself and results from a thermal deformation study.

Items.Authors: Ross Donnachie, Johan Schoeman
Items.Title: Digital revision of a geometric approach to group delay network synthesis
Items.Abstract: Presented is the adaptation of an analogue group delay network design technique to the digital domain. Direct design in the digital domain avoids any otherwise necessary and often deleterious transformations of the resultant system. This adaptation enables digital filter structures to be designed directly, with an equi-ripple error on the desired group delay response.

Items.Authors: Yuanpeng Gao
Items.Title: Digital twin modeling of large-aperture fast steering mirror for Space astronomical telescope
Items.Abstract: Driven by the key requirements of deep-space exploration, modern space astronomical telescopes are evolving toward larger apertures and longer focal lengths. To ensure high precision and stability in line-of-sight pointing, fast steering mirrors are increasingly application within these optical systems. Due to limited monitoring capabilities and insufficient temporal resolution within the orbital environment, models are required to possess the capability to accurately predict FSM states over finite time horizons. To address this challenge, this paper develops a horizon-adaptive hybrid digital-twin model that combines an incremental GRU rollout branch with a physics-guided residual branch. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to traditional neural network models, the proposed model achieves a 19% improvement in prediction accuracy for 500-step prediction tasks, thereby providing support for the subsequent state monitoring, and performance assessment of space mechanisms.

Items.Authors: François-Xavier Schmider, Olivier Lai, Hans-Peter Doerr, Max Görlach, Marcel Carbillet, Lyu Abe, Elora Lefebvre, Julien Dejonghe, Jean-Pierre Rivet, Markus Roth
Items.Title: Doppler imaging measurements in the visible with adaptive optics: improving and estimating the PSF for planetary atmosphere wind measurements
Items.Abstract: The AOC (Adaptive Optics at Calern) system is based on a 10x10 Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor and a 97-actuators deformable mirror, and installed on the 1-m C2PU telescope at Calern Observatory, near Nice. It aims at correcting turbulence for both stellar and planetary observations, in the visible (519nm) with the Doppler imager JOVIAL. Simulations of partial correction have been carried out to assess the performance of the system and the gain on accuracy in the velocity measurements.   We are developing performance evaluation tools for AOC, based on real-time telemetry. Additionally, we use a multi-frame blind deconvolution algorithm (MFBD) to estimate the point-spread function from a series of short exposures in the focal plane and compare it to the PSF retrieved from AO telemetry. We plan on using the reconstructed PSF to perform deconvolution on the Jupiter measurements to improve the wind profile determination.  We will present the methods, the observations and preliminary results

Items.Authors: Amir Ebadati Bazkiaei, Tayyaba Zafar, Nuria Lorente, Arihant Raidani
Items.Title: DustRover: a Python package for modelling dust extinction curves (phase I)
Items.Abstract: We introduce DustRover, an open-source Python package designed to model dust extinction curves using multi-wavelength observations. DustRover supports optical/NIR spectroscopy, broadband photometry, and X-ray data within a unified framework, enabling robust analysis of spectral energy distributions. Its modular design separates data management, dust models, and MCMC-based statistical fitting, providing flexibility for both standard and custom extinction parametrisations. The package is highly user-oriented, using simple YAML configuration files and offering built-in visualisation tools for SEDs and extinction curves. We present the Phase One capabilities of DustRover, show applications to real GRB and QSO datasets, and outline planned advancements towards a fully automated dust-analysis pipeline.

Items.Authors: Juan P. Gil, Pedro Silva, Gaspar Fabrega, Nicolas Miranda
Items.Title: ELIANA: an open source library for observatory log analytics
Items.Abstract: ELIANA (Event Log and Incident Analysis) is an open-source Python library for log analytics, developed at the Paranal Observatory to support the analysis of instruments and telescopes. The library is built on top of pandas, allows dataset generation, ML modules, and parlogs-observations, a public dataset of logs for VLTI using the Auxiliary Telescopes distributed as Parquet files aggregated by instrument, time range, and subsystem. ELIANA provides machine learning modules including logistic-regression, Naive-Bayes, specialized tokenizers and NLP utilities. The library has been used to foster academic collaboration (graduate lectures, PhD work, internships) and is actively integrated in several operational tools at Paranal that combine logs with other data sources for troubleshooting and analysis. This contribution presents the architecture of ELIANA, describes the structure and intended use of the parlogs-observations dataset, and illustrates use cases for observatory operations.

Items.Authors: Alfred Miksch, Victoria Laidlaw, Olivier Fauvarque, Benoît Neichel, Ronny Ramlau
Items.Title: Enhanced nonlinear wavefront sensing for adaptive optics with a double iQuad sensor design
Items.Abstract: Advanced adaptive optics (AO) systems use Fourier-type wavefront sensing to correct optical distortions, and  the iQuad wavefront sensor (WFS) is a recent addition to this category. Its four-quadrant phase mask can detect  many wavefront features, but some components may be poorly seen, causing instability in the AO loop. A dual-  path setup using two differently oriented iQuad sensors addresses this limitation by suppressing poorly seen phase  components. To ensure accurate and stable iQuad wavefront sensing, a fast and efficient nonlinear Levenberg-  Marquardt (LM) algorithm is applied for wavefront estimation. Numerical simulations comparing single and  double iQuad configurations show that the dual-sensor approach offers significantly improved performance.

Items.Authors: S. Kendrew, K. Rowlands, M. Engesser, S. Noriega-Crespo, J. Aguilar, S. Alberts, T. Bell, A. Carter, M. Cracraft, M. Decleir, H. Diamond-Lowe, A. Dyrek, K. Gordon, D. Hines, B. Holler, K. Larson, D. Law, K. Murray, B. Nickson, B. O'Sullivan, A. Petric, M. Regan, G. Sloan, B. Sargent, S. Shenoy, B. Trahin, I. Wong
Items.Title: Enhancing the performance and capabilities of the MIRI instrument on JWST
Items.Abstract: MIRI, the Mid-Infrared Instrument on the James Webb Space Telescope, provides the only capability longward of 5 µm on the observatory. In this regime, it is providing order-of-magnitude improvements over past facilities in a wavelength range that is challenging or impossible to access from the ground. As such, MIRI occupies a unique parameter space and offers unparalleled capabilities in all areas of astrophysics. Several years into its operational lifetime, we continue to explore the full breadth of MIRI's potential and make operational improvements to MIRI to create new capabilities and enhance its scientific return. In this paper we will describe several such improvements, and their anticipated impact on MIRI and JWST science - focusing on improvements in detector noise performance, improved time-series capabilities, definition of new subarrays and a wide-field slitless spectroscopy mode.

Items.Authors: Lionel Clermont, Céline Michel, Quentin Chouffart, Yuchen Zhao, Emmanuel Mazy, Ines Fuente, Federico La China, Bertrand Fougnie
Items.Title: Ensuring reliability in space: a closer look at the need for testing multiple optical payload units
Items.Abstract: Spaceborne optical payloads must undergo extensive testing before launch, verifying performance against expectations and generating input data for in-flight software. Recently, a trend has emerged to build multiple units of the same instrument. These can be launched together, increasing the total field of view coverage, or consecutively, extending mission's lifetime beyond that of a single payload and benefiting from economies of scale. This raises a crucial question: Should each model undergo ground testing, or is it sufficient to test just one and apply the findings to all? This presentation will address this question, discussing test and calibration results of 3 supposedly identical payload versions, comparing parameters such as MTF, distortion, polarization spectral properties, and stray light. Our findings indicate that while initial testing offers valuable insights, significant variations among the models necessitate thorough testing of each unit, at least for certain parameters

Items.Authors: Konrad R. Skup, Miroslaw Rataj, Piotr Wawer, Mateusz Sobiecki, Konrad Rutkowski, Przemysław Nita, Grzegorz Szymański, Marianna Fulara, Marcin Sobolewski, Nils Thernstrom, Łukasz Kuryłowicz, Daniel Półtorak, Aleksandra Mirońska, Marek Winkler, Maurycy Ciarka, Adam Sikorski, Roland Ottensamer, Gerald Mösenlechner, Marko Mecina, Armin Luntzer, Warren Holmes, Renaud Goullioud, Mauro Focardi, Eduardo Medinaceli , Raoul Grimoldi
Items.Title: ESA ARIEL FGS: instrument design and implementation
Items.Abstract: In this paper we present the Fine Guiding System (FGS), one of two scientific instruments on board ESA’s ARIEL mission, scheduled for launch in 2029. ARIEL will study hundreds of exoplanets to characterize their atmospheres, investigate chemical composition, cloud properties, and weather variability. FGS serves a dual purpose: it delivers dedicated scientific measurements through three photometric channels and a low-resolution near-infrared spectrometer, while also supporting the spacecraft with ultra-precise pointing. Following the instrument Critical Design Review (iCDR), the FGS has entered the phase of engineering qualification model integration and flight model preparation, marking a major step toward mission readiness.

Items.Authors: Ángela Hernández Delgado, Jorge Quintero Nehrkorn, Fernando Merlos-García, Josué Barrera Martín, Claudia Ruiz de Galarreta, Peter Dr Caligari, Manuel Collados Vera, Carmen Marillai Barreto Cabrera, Hector Socas-Navarro, Sergio Javier Gonzalez Manrique, Miguel Núñez Cagigal
Items.Title: EST Data Centre: challenges
Items.Abstract: The European Solar Telescope (EST) is a 4.2-meter solar facility planned to operate seven instruments: three TIS/FBI systems, three IFS-M units, and the EMBER IFS-S. EST is expected to generate around 169 GiB/s and about 2.7 PiB of data per day, posing major challenges in both data rate and data volume. The data flow from the instruments will require high-performance connectivity at the telescope, while the projected ~80 PiB per year cannot be efficiently handled by a single monolithic data center due to cost, scalability, and reliability limitations. As a result, the EST Data Center (EST-DC) is conceived as a distributed European architecture that minimizes data movement and provides the necessary storage and computing resources, following the FAIR principles
